candidate.title: The Trapdoor and Toto
candidate.text:
Toto slips from my grip as the floor shudders, the cyclone's breath ripping through the room. I lunge for Toto under the bed, my fingers brushing his warm coat and snagging at nothing as he darts deeper into the shadows. He squeezes behind the bed’s leg and scrambles for the bedskirt, tiny paws slipping in the dust. I plant my feet and lean, catching him by the scruff and lifting him free just as a gust rattles the door frame.

Aunt Em’s voice cuts through the wind, sharp with fear but clear with command. “Dorothy, the cellar—now!” She yanks the cellar ladder door wide and kicks at the trapdoor with her heel, sending it banging down a shout of timber and gloom. The room tilts again; Toto’s small body trembles in my arms as I carry him toward the cellar’s cool shadow. Em begins sliding down first, her skirt catching on a rung, and her breath comes fast and short—she’s not waiting for permission, just moving.

I gather Toto close and take a quick step, then another, aiming for the open hatch. Toto peeks from my chest, nose quivering at the cold air of the cellar’s mouth. The floor lurches and a final gust shoves me sideways; I catch myself with a hand braced on a chair, Toto clutched tight, and I keep moving toward Aunt Em.

The trapdoor yawns wide as Em disappears into the cellar, the edge of the world dropping away into cool, pressed air. My legs burn, my breath hitches, but I don’t slow. I reach Aunt Em’s glow at the bottom, Toto tucked against my ribs as I lower myself into the cool dark and the safe hush beneath the farmhouse.
